name: Apple Contacts
description: Apple Contacts is Apple's local and iCloud-backed address book for people, organizations, phone numbers, email addresses, postal addresses, groups, relationships, social profiles, and contact notes.
agentUseSummary: Apple Contacts cannot yet be connected through Relay. Apple documents native Contacts-framework access with per-device permission and separately supports account authorization or an app-specific password for compatible third-party iCloud Contacts clients, but it publishes no Relay-ready server API, Contacts OAuth scope, enrollment path, or frozen CardDAV lifecycle contract; the product must choose and validate an authority architecture first.

blocked.label: Connect Apple Contacts
blocked.description: Connect remains unavailable until Relay selects and accepts a supported native or delegated server authority model.

blocked.label: Collect Apple credentials
blocked.description: Apple Account passwords, app-specific passwords, verification codes, cookies, session tokens, and private framework material are never collected.

blocked.label: Read contacts
blocked.description: People, organizations, names, phone numbers, email and postal addresses, birthdays, relationships, social profiles, groups, containers, and notes remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Change contacts or use raw interfaces
blocked.description: Creating, updating, deleting, grouping, or merging contacts, private CardDAV discovery, scraping, device automation, arbitrary endpoints, and raw responses are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Apple Contacts action is enabled before a supported authority architecture and representative acceptance.

runtimeSupport.description: No Apple Contacts wrapper is mounted before the local-versus-server authority architecture is frozen.
No Apple Contacts wrapper is mounted before the local-versus-server authority architecture is frozen.

providerSetup.blocker: Apple's Contacts framework runs inside an Apple-platform app, requests explicit user permission, can expose a user-selected limited contact subset, and needs an additional entitlement for notes. Apple's current support guidance also permits compatible third-party apps to authorize iCloud Contacts access, or fall back to a broad app-specific password, but public developer documentation does not identify Contacts scopes, REST or CardDAV endpoints, client registration, token lifecycle, quotas, or server semantics for that supported-app flow.
providerSetup.nextAction: The product and security owners should select either a Mac-local Contacts-framework connector using limited-contact selection where possible or a provider-approved server authorization contract. The exclusive acceptance task must then obtain Apple entitlement or enrollment evidence, run consent on a representative account, verify exact contact authority, revocation, schema redaction, notes exclusion, quotas, change history, offline behavior, and disconnect denial, and return the frozen contract before implementation.

evidence.supports: Apple documents native Contacts-store access with explicit user authorization and a separate entitlement for reading or writing contact notes.

Apple's local CNContactStore can fetch and save contacts, groups, and containers, enumerate all contacts, observe changes, and execute save requests, establishing sensitive local read/write authority.
Apple supports limiting an app to a subset of contacts selected by the user, a least-authority option that must be considered for a local connector.

Apple states compatible third-party apps can request Apple Account authorization for iCloud Contacts and users can revoke the app under Account Data Sharing, without publishing a Contacts developer endpoint contract on that page.
Apple documents broad app-specific passwords as a fallback for iCloud Mail, Calendar, and Contacts; they require two-factor authentication and support revocation but are not contact-scoped.
